overview:
Collect IIS metrics aggregated across all of your sites, or on a per-site basis. The IIS Agent check collects metrics for active connections, bytes sent and received, request count by HTTP method, and more. It also sends a service check for each site, letting you know whether it's up or down.

**Minimum Agent version:** 6.0.0
setup:
### Installation

The IIS check is packaged with the Agent. To start gathering your IIS metrics and logs, [install the Agent][2] on your IIS servers.

#### Host

To configure this check for an Agent running on a host:

##### Metric collection

1. Edit the `iis.d/conf.yaml` file in the [Agent's `conf.d` directory][3] at the root of your [Agent's configuration directory][4] to start collecting your IIS site data. See the [sample iis.d/conf.yaml][5] for all available configuration options.

2. [Restart the Agent][6] to begin sending IIS metrics to Datadog.

**Note**: Versions 2.14.0 or later of this check use a new implementation for metric collection, which requires Python 3. For hosts that are unable to use Python 3, or if you would like to use a legacy version of this check, refer to the following [config][11].

##### Log collection

1. Collecting logs is disabled by default in the Datadog Agent, enable it in your `datadog.yaml` file:

   ```yaml
   logs_enabled: true
   ```

2. Add this configuration block to your `iis.d/conf.yaml` file to start collecting your IIS Logs:

   ```yaml
   logs:
     - type: file
       path: C:\inetpub\logs\LogFiles\W3SVC1\u_ex*
       service: myservice
       source: iis
   ```

    Change the `path` and `service` parameter values and configure them for your environment. See the [sample iis.d/conf.yaml][5] for all available configuration options.

3. [Restart the Agent][6].

**Note**: Ensure the `datadog-agent` user has read and execute access to tail the log files you want to collect from. When IIS creates a new sub-folder (such as when a new site is created), the permissions of the parent folder are not automatically inherited. See [Permission issues tailing log files][12] for more information.


### Validation

[Run the Agent's status subcommand][7] and look for `iis` under the Checks section.

metrics.name: iis.app_pool.recycle.count
metrics.description: The number of times that the application pool has been recycled since Windows Process Activation Service (WAS) started.

metrics.name: iis.app_pool.state
metrics.description: The current status of the application pool (1 - Uninitialized, 2 - Initialized, 3 - Running, 4 - Disabling, 5 - Disabled, 6 - Shutdown Pending, 7 - Delete Pending).

metrics.name: iis.app_pool.uptime
metrics.description: The length of time, in seconds, that the application pool has been running since it was started.

metrics.name: iis.errors.locked
metrics.description: The number of locked errors per second (typically reported as an HTTP 423 response code)

metrics.name: iis.errors.not_found
metrics.description: The number of not found errors per second (typically reported as an HTTP 404 response code)

metrics.name: iis.httpd_request_method.delete
metrics.description: The number of DELETE requests per second

metrics.name: iis.httpd_request_method.get
metrics.description: The number of GET requests per second

metrics.name: iis.httpd_request_method.head
metrics.description: The number of HEAD requests per second

metrics.name: iis.httpd_request_method.options
metrics.description: The number of OPTIONS requests per second

metrics.name: iis.httpd_request_method.post
metrics.description: The number of POST requests per second

metrics.name: iis.httpd_request_method.put
metrics.description: The number of PUT requests per second

metrics.name: iis.httpd_request_method.trace
metrics.description: The number of TRACE requests per second

metrics.name: iis.net.bytes_rcvd
metrics.description: The number of bytes received per second

metrics.name: iis.net.bytes_sent
metrics.description: The number of bytes served per second

metrics.name: iis.net.bytes_total
metrics.description: The total number of bytes transferred per second

metrics.name: iis.net.connection_attempts
metrics.description: The number of connection attempts since service startup

metrics.name: iis.net.connection_attempts_sec
metrics.description: The number of connection attempts per second

metrics.name: iis.net.files_rcvd
metrics.description: The number of files received per second

metrics.name: iis.net.files_sent
metrics.description: The number of files sent per second

metrics.name: iis.net.num_connections
metrics.description: The number of active connections

metrics.name: iis.requests.cgi
metrics.description: The number of Common Gateway Interface requests executed per second

metrics.name: iis.requests.isapi
metrics.description: The number of ISAPI requests executed per second

metrics.name: iis.uptime
metrics.description: The amount of time the IIS server has been running

metrics.name: iis.users.anon
metrics.description: The number of requests from users over an anonymous connection per second

metrics.name: iis.users.nonanon
metrics.description: The number of requests from users over a non-anonymous connection per second

serviceChecks.name: Site Up
serviceChecks.description: Returns `CRITICAL` if the uptime for a site is 0 and `OK` otherwise. The site uptime is collected via Windows Performance Data Helper using the 'Web Service(*)\Service Uptime' counter

serviceChecks.name: App Pool Up
serviceChecks.description: Returns `CRITICAL` if the tagged app_pool is down and `OK` otherwise.

monitors.title: Request number is high
monitors.description: HTTP requests are sent to your web application hosted by IIS. This monitor tracks anomalies in the request count to detect unusual patterns or changes in traffic to identify potential issues in your web application's performance or behavior.
monitors.query: avg(last_4h):anomalies(avg:iis.httpd_request_method.get{*} by {site} + avg:iis.httpd_request_method.put{*} by {site} + avg:iis.httpd_request_method.head{*} by {site} + avg:iis.httpd_request_method.delete{*} by {site} + avg:iis.httpd_request_method.options{*} by {site}, 'agile', 2, direction='both', alert_window='last_15m', interval=60, count_default_zero='true', seasonality='daily') >= 1

monitors.title: 404 errors is high
monitors.description: Not all the requests headed to your application will end correctly. This monitor tracks anomalies in the 4xx HTTP response codes from the IIS Server to provide insights into unusual client errors.
monitors.query: avg(last_4h):anomalies(avg:iis.errors.not_found{*} by {site}, 'agile', 2, direction='above', alert_window='last_15m', interval=60, count_default_zero='true', seasonality='daily') >= 1

monitors.title: Locked errors is high
monitors.description: Resources requested by a client might be not accessible. This monitor tracks the number of locked errors in IIS to identify anomalies based on the historical pattern of error counts.
monitors.query: avg(last_4h):anomalies(avg:iis.errors.locked{*} by {site}, 'agile', 2, direction='above', alert_window='last_15m', interval=60, count_default_zero='true', seasonality='daily') >= 1
